description: Committee recommends $100,000 for three cultural organizations.
Funding supports Saskatchewan Jazz Festival rebrand.
Also funds On Board Staging Company lighting equipment.

chips.text: Funding benefits Saskatchewan Jazz Festival, On Board Staging, Saskatoon Jazz Society.
Delegates from Jazz Festival and On Board Staging thanked City for support.

speakers.name: Shannon Josdal
speakers.summary: Shannon Josdal addressed committee indicating that SaskTel has advised that it is withdrawing the title sponsorship as of 2026 and that the Saskatchewan Jazz Festival will require a rebrand.
said: Rebranding is needed as SaskTel will not renew title sponsorship for 2026.
Award covers 42% of rebranding costs, avoiding impact on programming.
All project consultants and suppliers are local to Saskatoon.

description: Committee recommends Council note three reports.
Monitors Saskatoon's Official Community Plan and growth annually.
Details 23 OCP amendments from 2021-2024, many for housing.
Tracks residential, commercial, and industrial development.

chips.text: Major land developers in Saskatoon provide data for growth monitoring.

description: East Side Leisure Centre will be a standalone facility on a shared campus.
Project will use a design-build approach for construction.
Construction is expected to take 30 to 36 months.

chips.text: High school students and public user groups will access the new leisure centre.
Over 5,000 community members provided feedback through a survey.
Administration will report back on public engagement results in Q2 2025.

description: Committee receives requested report list with timelines.
Updates are provided twice yearly.
Residents oppose 100-foot 5G cell tower in Canonsmith Park near homes.
Residents request city send non-concurrence letter to Industry Canada.
City policy on antenna systems is outdated, limiting local jurisdiction.

chips.text: 110 residents signed a petition opposing the cell tower proposal.
Why the tower must be directly in front of homes was not explained.
Public consultation meeting was an 'open house' where residents had to stand.

description: City administration will review the antenna systems policy.
Review considers changing technology and consultation processes.

chips.text: Council debated the policy's vague definition of a 'contentious issue'.
Residents living directly across from Canonsmith Park are most impacted.
Why the cell tower must be directly in front of homes remains unanswered.
Residents presented petition and 110 signatures opposing cell tower.

speakers.name: Canon Smith Park
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Cell Tower
said: The cell tower in Canon Smith Park does not comply with outdated code number six to 15.
Saskatoon Council's antenna systems policy is outdated by 11 years, last reviewed in 2014.
Requests a special session for council members to address cell tower issues and health effects.
